description: A companion for vcClk that takes its tempo voltage and gives seven divisions of it, each as a 0-10V square wave and as a tempo voltage of its own

params.text: Restarts all seven clocks together when pressed

inputs.text: The tempo everything here works from, 1V for every 60 bpm, where the maker's manual says 1V for every 50 bpm
Subtracts from the incoming tempo before the square waves are made, at the same 1V for every 60 bpm; the seven tempo voltage outputs are taken before this is applied, so it moves the pulses alone
Restarts all seven clocks together on a rising edge, so they line up again; any voltage away from zero counts as high

outputs.text: A 0-10V square wave at one pulse per beat of the incoming tempo, half of each cycle high
A 0-10V square wave at one pulse every two beats of the incoming tempo, half of each cycle high
A 0-10V square wave at one pulse every three beats of the incoming tempo, half of each cycle high
A 0-10V square wave at one pulse every four beats of the incoming tempo, half of each cycle high
A 0-10V square wave at one pulse every five beats of the incoming tempo, half of each cycle high
A 0-10V square wave at one pulse every seven beats of the incoming tempo, half of each cycle high
A 0-10V square wave at one pulse every nine beats of the incoming tempo, half of each cycle high
The incoming tempo passed on as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
Half the incoming tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
A third of the incoming tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
A quarter of the incoming tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
A fifth of the incoming tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
A seventh of the incoming tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm
A ninth of the incoming tempo as a voltage, 1V for every 60 bpm

notes: nothing at all comes out until a tempo voltage is patched to the gold-ringed input; there is no knob here to set a tempo with
the seven clocks run free of one another and only line up after a reset, so patch the reset output of vcClk into the reset input here

inputs.0:
unipolar · continuous · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2: high above 0V · stepped · one channel only
